# `Q-10-1` — Template Parse Error

> A Quarto document template failed to parse.

## What this means

Quarto's document template engine reads Pandoc-flavored
templates (`$variable$`, `$if(x)$...$endif$`, `$partial(name)$`,
`$x/pipe$`). This error fires when the engine cannot parse a
template at all — usually because of an unbalanced delimiter,
an unrecognized control construct, or a syntactically malformed
expression.

Without a parsable template, the surrounding render cannot
continue: there is no fallback rendering for a template that
cannot be read.

## Why this happens

Common causes:

- **A `$` that was meant as a literal** in non-template text.
  Literal dollar signs must be doubled: `$$`.
- **An unbalanced control block** — `$if(x)$` with no
  `$endif$`, or vice versa.
- **A typo in a control keyword** (`$endfi$` instead of
  `$endif$`).

## How to fix

Read the error message — the engine names the position where
parsing failed. Common fixes: balance the `$if/$endif$` pair,
escape literal `$` characters, correct the keyword spelling.

## Related

- `Q-10-2` — undefined variable: parsing succeeded, but a
  reference was unresolved.
